#1264. Aston Villa Made Massive Error With New Maatsen Deal After Galatasaray Stinker

Aston Villa fell to a sixth game without a victory as Galatasaray scored a late winner to claim victory in the Champions League on Tuesday evening.

The Villans started strongly but registered just a single shot on target across 90 minutes, as substitute Deniz Gul headed home the winning goal while being kicked in the face to grab all three points for the hosts.

The defeat means that Villa have lost their last two Champions League games, and they are now winless in six games across all competitions, meaning Unai Emery must begin to look at ways to change the team's fortunes after a slow start to the campaign.

Villa have been rocked by a number of injury issues across the team this season, including long-term absentee Amadou Onana, while summer signings Aaron Wan-Bissaka and Matteo Ruggeri were both absent from the game due to knocks, as was first-choice right-back Matty Cash, who is dealing with a concussion.

That means that left-back Ian Maatsen was the only natural full-back option fit and available for the game, but he turned in a shocking performance on the night as Villa struggled to create going forward and looked relatively shaky at the back.

The Netherlands international has recently signed a new contract at Villa Park to extend his stay in the Midlands until 2032, and described the decision as an 'easy one', with working under Emery one of his main factors for signing.

“It was an easy decision, the way the club grows in their environment. I have the opportunity to show my qualities, Unai gives me the confidence to play my own game. It is such a good moment and a really proud moment to extend my contract with this beautiful club.”

But after his performance in Istanbul, and with Villa's problems defensively so far this season, the manager will surely be questioning the decision to commit to him in the long-term and essentially confirm that he will be first-choice for the foreseeable future.

Maatsen started in his preferred left-back role with Tyron Mings alongside him and Johan Manzambi ahead of him. But while the team were rather unfortunate to concede in the way they did, they were lucky that it didn't come earlier in the game.

During the game, Maatsen lost possession 21 times, failed to successfully make a tackle, won just 2 of his 13 duel attempts, was dribbled past twice, and conceded two fouls. That shocker of a performance earned him a measly 4/10 rating from the Birmingham Mail, the lowest of any player (alongside Manzambi and Nicolas Jackson).

This was his 7th consecutive start for the team too, so using rust or a lack of rhythm simply won't stand either. He's simply showing that he just isn't good enough to do what the manager wants from him.

After losing Lucas Digne to PSG in the summer, the hope was that Maatsen could step up in his place and take over the mantle, while competing alongside Ruggeri.

But Ruggeri has struggled to adapt to English football so far, and Maatsen hasn't shown anywhere near enough to suggest that he should keep that role. Despite signing ten new players in the summer, a left-back should now be right at the top of their priorities.

Alejandro Garnacho was by far the worst and most pointless signing of the window, with the Argentine not making the bench in Istanbul despite Emery naming two goalkeepers and leaving an empty spot on his team sheet. But there is at least an argument that he hasn't really been given an opportunity.

Maatsen has, and he's failed to take it. For the club to then hand him a new long-term contract anyway is a grave error if he performs this way, and someone must take accountability by ensuring he is replaced in January.

The Dutch forward has had a brilliant time in Italy.

#1263. Ian Holloway SACKED by Swindon two days after trying to confront angry fans in feisty full-time scenes at Newport - with Premier League cult hero claiming club's training ground is haunted

Published: 05:52 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 10:57 EST, 23 November 2026

Ian Holloway has been sacked by Swindon just two days after attempting to confront angry fans following defeat to Newport on Saturday.

The journeyman manager had himself called the 2-0 loss on the road 'unforgivable' after he was taunted by home supporters chanting that he would be 'sacked in the morning' after the result.

Holloway had intended to go down the tunnel after the final whistle, and passed the away stand on his route out, taking off his cap as he held up his hands in resignation.

But as boos rained down on him, the 63-year-old could not resist the urge to engage, looking to answer back to the fans before he was restrained by security.

Last month, Holloway described himself as a 'dead man walking' with the Robins mired 17th in League Two, but Monday morning saw him despatched after two seasons in charge.

'Since joining the club towards the end of 2024, Ian has played an important role in stabilising our on-field position and helping the club make progress season upon season,' the Swindon statement announcing his departure read.

Saturdays eh.#STFC pic.twitter.com/1GL3blApwW

Ian Holloway was caught up in a clash with fans after Swindon's defeat to Newport County - shortly before he was sacked (Source: X/Loathed Stranger)

The journeyman manager oversaw two seasons at the club, saving them from relegation in 2024-25

'However, following careful consideration of recent results and performances, the club believes that now is the right time to take a different direction.

'This has not been an easy decision, but the board firmly believes that it is important to make difficult decisions when necessary, always with the best interests of Swindon Town at heart.'

Holloway cut a disillusioned figure at Rodney Parade as he gave a heartfelt assessment of his side's performance after defeat to the Exiles.

'It's devastating,' said Holloway. 'I'm bitterly disappointed. Did I expect my team to do that? Not in a million years.

'We're getting regular mistakes from almost everyone in that backline and in that midfield. We knew what type of game it was going to be. There's no excuses. I've just said to them "what on Earth do you think you're doing?" To start that way? It was so passive it was unforgivable.

'It's very painful at the minute. It'll come back at the manager in the end if I listen to all these people (from the stands).

'This is football. I've been in it a long time. This is my life.'

Holloway also questioned the desire of his players, continuing: 'Bitterly disappointed in all of them and disappointed for the fans. I get it, that didn't look like our team.

'They scored two ugly goals. All our chances that we had, normally we take them.

'Where's the fight? It's a local derby. I'm sorry, they've done their bits better than us.'

Holloway has endured an uneven stint at Swindon since 2024, saving the club from relegation in his first season but failing to challenge for the promotion places as time wore on.

Memorably, the former Crystal Palace and Queen's Park Rangers manager claimed that the training ground was haunted shortly after his arrival in Wiltshire.

Holloway had first suggested that there had been 'some strange things happening' after the club captain Ollie Clarke had ruptured his ankle in training, before enlisting his wife Kim to free spirits potentially trapped in the South West.

'I'm absolutely devastated so I'm going to try and cleanse the training ground area because people are telling me it's haunted,' Holloway said on BBC Radio Wiltshire in November 2024.

'There's a graveyard somewhere near. Honestly, I'm not joking.

'I think our training ground is very close to an ancient burial site so I'm going to get my wife to come up and say sorry to all these people and hopefully we'll have a bit more luck.'

#1262. Carrick weighs up stripping Bruno Fernandes of Man Utd captaincy

A defiant Michael Carrick refused to rule out stripping Bruno Fernandes of the captaincy as the Manchester United manager told his players to cut out their public sniping and start doing their talking on the pitch.

Carrick struck a bullish tone as he came out fighting and moved to reassert his authority after a tumultuous past fortnight that has left him battling to save his job ahead of Sunday’s must-win game against Bournemouth at Old Trafford.

The United manager began his press conference on Friday afternoon with a stirring five-and-a-half-minute monologue in which he issued an emotional call to arms to his players to demonstrate the values of hard work, sacrifice, humility and resilience that define the club.

Referencing Sir Matt Busby, Sir Alex Ferguson, Sir Bobby Charlton, Ryan Giggs and Wayne Rooney, Carrick warned there could be no “entitlement” culture in echoes of complaints from his predecessor Ruben Amorim.

United are actively considering their options in the event Carrick cannot quickly arrest a shocking start to the season that hit a new low with Wednesday’s 4-1 humiliation by Como. The likes of Julian Nagelsmann, Eddie Howe, Unai Emery, Fabian Hürzeler and Antonio Conte are in the frame.

But Carrick insisted he was “100 per cent” convinced he was the right man to take United forward and, while he claimed the dressing room was “not divided”, he has had to contend with first defender Lisandro Martínez and then Fernandes venting in public.

Martínez was fined and publicly apologised for an extraordinary tirade at Jason Wilcox, the director of football, and the Old Trafford board last week before Fernandes appeared to call out Carrick’s tactics in the wake of the Como debacle.

Carrick responded at the time to having his set-up and approach questioned by suggesting tactics count for little if players are unprepared to run.

Asked if he would consider taking the captaincy off Fernandes, Carrick said: “I’m just saying I’ll always – whatever the situation is – do what’s best for the club.”

Pressed on whether Fernandes’s comments were all the more insidious and divisive at a time when the manager was trying to pull the squad together so soon after Martínez’s outburst, Carrick added: “Yeah, the most important thing for me is the team.

“First and foremost is the squad, the dynamics in the squad. And again, it’s about the club. And I’ll always do what’s best for the club.”

Carrick, Wilcox and United chief executive Omar Berrada held a meeting with Martínez in the wake of his criticism but the manager would not be drawn on whether he had spoken with Fernandes and it remains to be seen if he will be captain or start against Bournemouth.

“If I’ve spoken to him or haven’t spoken to him, I don’t think this is the time to go into too much detail,” he said.

Carrick agreed that United collectively needed to stop turning on each other in public. “We need to move forward in the right direction. We need to do things that enable us to do that. That’s pretty clear,” he said.

“It [the dressing room] is not divided, no. We just need to get back to doing what we do best and we will.”

Separately, Carrick expressed sympathy for Fernandes over the “awful” burglary at his home on Wednesday night when he was in Italy, and said the club “are doing a lot of work to support Bruno and his family”.

Carrick is under huge pressure heading into Bournemouth but said he was happy to take the heat if it enabled his players to perform.

“It is my responsibility whatever goes on the pitch, and what we are as a group, and what we look like, and what we feel like,” he said. “I’ll hold that umbrella for me to get wet and for everyone else to stay dry.”

Nonetheless, Carrick admitted he was “hurting an awful lot” and that the team had to get back to showing the values and qualities that have underpinned the club’s historic success after a “really unacceptable” performance against Como and wider struggles. United have won two of 11 matches this season.

“I’m not entitled to be here,” Carrick said. “We’re not entitled to win. We’ve won in the past, we’ve got an incredible history, but that doesn’t mean you’re entitled to just win.

“I’m fully aware of that. It takes hard work, a lot of sacrifice. You’ve got to invest yourself in the club and you’ve got to do a lot of things that maybe aren’t so nice, but you’ve got to do it for each other, and you’ve got to win.

“It’s important we live up to that, and it’s important for me to push those values, and for our supporters to feel that moving forward.

“We’ve kind of lost our way a bit if I’m honest, and we will get it back. I’m totally confident we’ll get it back. Respect this club, respect what it takes, because it’s very important to me.”

Carrick added that he was inspired by the values of “humility, hard work, resilience, sacrifice and pride” embodied by the likes of Busby, Ferguson, Charlton, Giggs and Rooney.

“We can never lose that, and I won’t let us lose that,” he said. “We’ve had it for a spell, I feel very strongly about that. It inspires me a lot to live up to that and keep driving that with the players.

“There’s a resilience about this club that’s been shown for a long time. Whether that’s bouncing back from adversity, comebacks, late goals, success, sustaining success, there’s a resilience in this club that runs very deep.”

Carrick was trailed by a camera crew from Amazon Prime as he entered the media auditorium at Manchester United’s Carrington training base at 1.30pm on Friday.

There have been plenty of dark moments at Old Trafford in the post-Sir Alex Ferguson era. But the difference this season is that any internal drama will soon be available for public consumption after the decision to allow cameras into a once-sacrosanct dressing room.

Whether Carrick will see out the next week, let alone a season being captured by filmmakers from Amazon’s All Or Nothing series, who probably cannot believe their luck at the unfolding crisis, remains to be seen. He certainly needs a big reaction against Bournemouth at Old Trafford at the very least.

But it became clear as he began his press conference with an emotional 5½-minute monologue that he would not go down without a fight.

🗣️ Commitment. Resilience. Teamwork. Michael's powerful message in full 👇 https://t.co/vWwJt1fW47

This was partly Carrick reasserting his own authority after a couple of weeks in which two senior players – defender Lisandro Martínez and captain Bruno Fernandes – decided to go public with their grievances and the team delivered a performance in the 4-1 hammering by Como that was up there with the very worst.

But a stony-faced Carrick was also sending a message to his squad to quit their public sniping and start pulling together for a wider cause. Moreover, to put the club and the team before yourself and your individual needs and complaints.

It was interesting that he used the word “entitlement”. His predecessor, Ruben Amorim, had uttered that same word to attack what he felt was an “entitlement culture” at the club and Carrick has evidently come to a similar conclusion.

"I think it's the feeling of entitlement that we have in our club" Ruben Amorim says some of the players at Manchester United may need a bit of a reality check 🎙️ https://t.co/PiJWML3TeH

In truth, so many of the post-Ferguson managers have spoken in similar ways – certainly Ole Gunnar Solskjaer, Jose Mourinho and Ralf Rangnick.

Listening to Carrick repeatedly talking about the need for humility, hard work, pride, sacrifice and resilience was a reminder of how the values that were once taken for granted at this football club have steadily been eroded.

Wayne Rooney said this week that United’s players were “selfish” and “babies”. Many top players over the years have been selfish but it helped drive them and, in turn, their team to great heights, but the same cannot be said about the current bunch.

Carrick spoke about trying to rediscover something that is “lost” at the moment. Whether they can is a big if. Opponents aside, the only winners at the moment from United’s latest crisis are Amazon.

It feels at times as if it can be a long way away but it doesn’t take too much to flip the other way and we’re more than capable of doing that, I totally believe that.

We will. We’ll win football matches and we’ve got a very tough one on Sunday [against Bournemouth].

Very, very good team that we’re playing again and I’m not suggesting that becomes an easy game because it doesn’t. We’ve got to respect the game, respect what it takes to win.

We’ve spoken. There are always conversations going on. It’s pretty obvious how we’re all feeling. A reaction, a reaction from me.

The responsibility for me in this position is to lead. It is my responsibility, whatever goes on the pitch and what we look like, what we feel like.

Carrick had clearly thought hard about how he was going to tackle that today and what message he wanted to get across. The long and short of it was that the United manager was issuing a call to arms to his players to pull their finger out, respect the badge and start showing the kind of values of humility and hard work that the club is founded on. By name checking the likes of Sir Alex Ferguson and Matt Busby he was speaking about the people who exemplified the values United are all about

The foundations of this football club and values have been etched down for many years.

I totally understand and I get every single one of them. It comes down to being humble, to hard work and being really proud to live up to those values.

There is a resilience about this football club that has been shown for a long, long time. Whether that’s bouncing back from adversity, comebacks, late goals, sustaining success, there is a resilience to this football club that runs very, very deep.

No definitive answer from Carrick, who says he wants to do what is best for the football club.

There ends the broadcast section of the press conference after about 15 minutes.

Definitely a change in communication strategy from Carrick, speaking from the heart rather than waiting for questions.

My responsibility is to get a team on the pitch that represents this football club, represents the supporters and they can be proud of it with the identity that we show.

We have gone away from that just recently in certain games, which I’m fully aware of and definitely doing something about.

I think it’s important we all recognise that. I certainly recognise it. Our supporters of are the utmost importance to me and this football club.

For them to feel like they felt for five months at the start of the year and have that about us, that connection and that real vigour, intensity and enjoyment and passion is something we need to get back to.

Carrick says the dressing room is “not divided” but says it’s pretty clear the squad and everyone have to pull together and stop speaking out like has happened in public in response to questions about Martinez and Fernandes’ outbursts.

Principles are so important. We can win games, lose games, hopefully not but it can happen.

It’s how you do it and what it feels like is important for me. That the spirit and togetherness is there. It will be there. I’m working on solutions to move us forward.

I haven’t invented anything new, it’s the make-up of any good football team. You have to earn the right to be better than your opponent, that’s not changed and it never changes.

He says loads of conversations have been going on. He says it’s his responsibility “to lead” and that “I’ll hold that umbrella for me to get wet and keep everyone else dry.”

Carrick adds on the Fernandes burglary. “It’s an awful thing to go through and we’re doing a lot of things to support him and his family.”

It was never about Ryan Giggs, it was never about Ryan Giggs, it was about Manchester United.

Wayne Rooney is top goalscorer of this football club. His biggest thing was playing for the team, sacrificing for the team and what was good for Manchester United.

Sir Alex Ferguson is the best manager of all-time. The greatest, for me. And working for him, his main priority was Manchester United.

Sir Matt [Busby] and Sir Bobby [Charlton], their resilience was beyond belief what they showed and how they rebuilt this football club. It was based on being humble, having humility and hard work. We can never lose that and I won’t let us lose that.

We’ve lost our way if I’m totally honest but we’ll get back what it takes.

Carrick has come in, trailed by the Amazon cameras, sat down and made an address for five minutes before taking any questions. He acknowledges it’s not been good enough or what the club expects and that it’s got to get better. He’s talking about rebuilding this club based on humility, values and hard work and won’t let that go and that it inspires him going forward. “Yeah we’re in a moment where it’s not going well but we need to show exactly what it means and respect what it means to be here and what it takes to win,” he said. “You’re not entitled to win. It takes hard work.”

I think it’s important... recently we haven’t had a good time I think that’s obvious, I totally accept that.

We had five months of relative success and I was happy with many things I was seeing.

We haven’t done well enough recently. Wednesday was a bad night for a lot of reasons, it really hurt a lot, it hurt me to see how the game panned out.

As I said after the game, it was unacceptable.

Hopefully he will be in position by half-past, but it is not unlike managers to keep everyone waiting.

My name has been linked with numerous clubs, but there are currently no negotiations at an advanced stage.

Following a wonderful and successful spell in charge of Napoli, I will take the time I need to consider how and when to return to management. It will be a carefully considered decision, one I will make when I believe the conditions are right.

I have read reports of financial demands and requests for full control that I have supposedly already made to the clubs mentioned, as well as reservations about what has been described as my “strong personality”. These reports are unfounded, as there is currently no concrete basis for such assessments.

Should a concrete opportunity arise, that will be the time to hold discussions with the club concerned and jointly consider the terms of a potential agreement, with due regard for both parties’ needs and the qualities and approach that define my work as a manager.

Until then, any assumptions about my demands and my professional future remain speculation and cannot be treated as fact.

For all his brilliance and ruthlessness as a businessman, Sir Jim Ratcliffe has yet to convince that he has any feel for football. Just look at the performance of Ineos’s other prize assets this season: Lausanne-Sport lie 12th in the 12-team Swiss top flight after one win in 10, and Nice are a distant 13th in Ligue 1, having burnt through eight different managers during the petrochemical giant’s seven years in charge.

As James Ducker and Sam Dean explore in this piece, a succession of Manchester United managers have admonished their team for a lack of industry and athleticism. A number of factors may be to blame: recruitment errors, paralysing pressure and a bad dressing-room culture among them. It is time to get back to basics.

Michael Carrick is not one of the Premier League’s more loquacious managers but supporters will be interested in what he has to say at his pre-Bournemouth press conference this afternoon.

The Manchester United manager is under severe pressure after a run of no wins in seven games across all competitions, and senior players are talking out of school in post-game interviews.

Just when it appeared a line had been drawn under Lisandro Martinez taking on technical director Jason Wilcox, Bruno Fernandes reached for a petrol can and poured more fuel on the flames.

Speaking after the dismal 4-1 Champions League defeat by Como, Fernandes called out Carrick and his coaching staff for their tactical approach, specifically a reluctance to press opponents aggressively in a man-to-man fashion.

Carrick, by his own very measured standards, delivered a pointed response.

“We actually were half-pressed man to man in the second half and then conceded a goal from that,” he said. “And there’s a little bit on whatever system you play, whatever tactics you play, if you don’t run, and you don’t run forward, and you don’t run back, you ain’t going to win.”

Their opponents on Sunday are Bournemouth, who after a lean run of results under Marco Rose have just dispatched Sunderland for their first league victory of the season, and the mighty AC Milan in the Europa League.

Things do not get easier for United, who go to Stamford Bridge next weekend before a home game against Aston Villa before the November international break.

Telegraph Sport reported on Thursday that former Bayern Munich and Germany manager Julian Nagelsmann features prominently and is understood to want the job – as does Antonio Conte. United are also tracking Fabian Hurzeler while there is interest in Eddie Howe.

United are currently 13th in the table with seven points from seven games.

#1261. Gasperini: ‘A great moment for Roma to face the best’ ahead of PSG test

Gian Piero Gasperini says Roma’s trip to Paris Saint-Germain is “a great moment” to test themselves against the best, and admits the Lisbon defeat with Atalanta still leaves a bitter taste.

With quotes via TuttoMercatoWeb, the Roma coach was speaking at his pre-match press conference at the Parc des Princes, alongside Paulo Dybala, ahead of Wednesday’s Champions League clash. Kick-off is at 21:00 CET [20:00 GMT].

“It’s definitely a very, very good moment for us to be able to play this game against the strongest team,” Gasperini said. “What we’re thinking about most at the moment is putting in a high-level performance.

“It’s clear we have to measure ourselves against this team. It’s the first time we’ve faced them with Roma, so we’ll have to understand straight away on the pitch what their level is. It’s certainly very high, and we need to see how much we can counter their technique and their speed. Our aim is to reduce their effectiveness a little so that we can also play our own game.”

Roma go to Paris with four points from four games after dramatic defeats to Real Madrid and Manchester United. PSG, the holders, have won all four of theirs.

Gasperini insisted those losses shouldn’t affect his side’s confidence.

“This is what the Champions League is like. It’s the most important competition in the world, with the highest level,” he said. “You can put in very good performances, like we did against Real and Manchester, but then there are key moments, and the best players in the world are on the pitch and can decide games.

“We have to focus on producing that type of performance, because it gives you confidence, makes you grow and carries over into the league.”

This is not Gasperini’s first big night against PSG. In the 2020 quarter-final in Lisbon, his Atalanta side were leading going into the final minutes, but lost 2-1 to two late goals.

“That’s a game that’s still a bit hard to swallow, because of the ending,” he admitted. “We were down to 10 men in the final minutes because of Freuler’s injury and had no substitutions left. PSG brought on Mbappé, and he was decisive. But it’s still one of the highest moments in Atalanta’s history.

“This is a different type of game, because PSG are different. They’re much more of a team now, and that’s thanks to Luis Enrique. Roma are coming into this competition after several years away, which is different for us. It’s a league-phase game, and for us it’s a measure of what we’re doing.”

#1260. 2026/27 Premier League Table Without 'VAR Errors'

James is a Senior Editor for GIVEMESPORT with over eight years of experience in the industry. After graduating from the University of Southampton in 2016 with a degree in history, he joined the company as an Academy member in July 2017 and, after a short time working as a freelancer, was given a full-time role in February 2018.  He primarily covers the biggest stories in the football world but is also comfortable reporting on a variety of other sports including darts, golf, Formula 1, tennis, boxing and athletics. He has covered some massive events during his time at GIVEMESPORT, including numerous Champions League and World Cup finals, as well as the Olympics in 2020 and 2024.

Video Assistant Referee (VAR) has its fair share of critics. Introduced to the Premier League at the start of the 2019/20 season, the technology was designed to help the on-pitch officials and ensure matches were officiated seamlessly and without controversy.

However, it has not had the impact that it was intended to have. If anything, the number of refereeing controversies has gone up, and many high-profile names, including Roy Keane and Wayne Rooney, have lost patience and want to see VAR scrapped.

But what would the 2026/27 Premier League table look like if every refereeing decision was correct? After every matchday in England's top tier, Squawka asks their followers to vote on controversial VAR decisions and whether the right decision was made or not.

Using that data, they have created a Premier League table without VAR errors following matchday 11, and it makes for interesting reading.

The table has been compiled on the basis that penalties, should they have been awarded, would have been converted.

Sunderland have had a dismal start to the campaign. The Black Cats, who are competing in the Conference League after finishing seventh in 2025/26, are currently 18th in the Premier League, having picked up nine points from their opening 11 games. They can be grateful for VAR that their troubles aren't any worse, though, as they would be rock bottom without its errors.

Crystal Palace would be second bottom, with Manchester United rounding out the relegation places, even after Leny Yoro had his red card overturned after he was wrongly sent off in a 4-0 defeat at Anfield in Mauricio Pochettino's first game. Nottingham Forest, who are currently 17th in the Premier League, would be two points better off, though that wouldn't change their position.

Back in September, Forest and Tottenham Hotspur drew 0-0 at the City Ground. VAR is adjudged to have wrongly intervened to disallow Neco Williams' goal for the home side. The Premier League released a statement explaining the goal had been ruled out for handball, but many felt the footage was inconclusive and not clear and obvious. Had VAR made the right decision, Forest would have won 1-0.

Coventry City currently sit 14th in the table, which is one place higher than they would be without technology. Fulham also find themselves one place higher than they should be, which should mean newly promoted Ipswich Town should be two places higher and in 14th instead

Hull City have had a tremendous start and currently sit 11th in the table, but they would be a point and one place worse off without VAR errors.

Tottenham Hotspur would find themselves one place worse off down in 11th if VAR decisions were correct, though their recent uptick in form should see them consolidate on their top half place soon enough. Newcastle United currently find themselves in 13th in the table, which is also the case in this table.

Premier League Table Without VAR Errors (20-11)

Everton are currently sitting in ninth and propping up the top half of the table with 16 points and a -2 goal difference from their opening 11 games. But while their points total wouldn't have changed, the VAR decisions being correct would have them a place lower thanks to the fact Aston Villa should move up three places - the most of any side.

Leeds have had a strong start to the season, but they would be one place worse off in eighth in the table without any VAR errors, while Bournemouth would be dropping down to 7th in the table, two places lower than their place in the Europa League qualification spots right now.

Second only to Villa, Chelsea would be another big winner in the top-half without VAR. While they currently sit eighth, with questions being rasied about their defence - as well as Xabi Alonso's management - technology has denied them of three points, meaning they could be up to sixth and level on points with Brentford, who are above them.

Manchester City would be two points worse off in fourth place, on 19 points, if VAR errors were fixed. They won 1-0 at Old Trafford thanks to Erling Haaland's winner. ProRef released a statement revealing that the goal should have been ruled out due to Enzo Fernandez being in an offside position. Without that goal, the match would've ended in a goalless draw.

Despite still being a relatively new feature of the game, VAR has already led to numerous errors in football, but which ones have been the worst?

Brighton would still be second place on 22 points, but they would be sharing that points tally with Liverpool, who wouldn't have lost against Arsenal without VAR errors.

The Reds felt aggrieved that they weren't given a penalty when Alexander Isak's shirt was tugged by Jurrien Timber in the box, preventing him from having a header at goal. If VAR had made the right decision, Liverpool would've been given a spot-kick, and it is assumed they would have scored and that the spoils would have been shared.

Despite that, Mikel Arteta's side would still be well clear at the top of the table without VAR errors.

Premier League Table Without VAR Errors (10-1)

#1259. People entering old age now have better memory than their parents did

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Miryam Naddaf is a reporter for Nature in London.

Improvements in education, lifestyle and health during early life are slowing rates of cognitive decline in older people.Credit: Laura Olivas/Getty

People born later in the twentieth century have a better memory when they enter old age and experience slower cognitive decline than do those born earlier, according to a study1 published in Nature Medicine on 17 November. The analysis offers clues about why dementia rates have fallen by 13% per decade over the past 27 years in Europe and the United States2.

The researchers analysed data from memory tests that required participants to recall lists of words. The study included 219,000 people aged 50 and older who were born between 1910 and 1964, and tracked changes in their scores over three decades. These list-based tests are commonly used to screen for dementia and Alzheimer’s disease.

Consistent with previous studies3, people born more recently entered old age with better memory performance compared with those born in earlier generations. A ten-year jump in birth date was associated with a 10% higher memory score at the age of 60. Memory decline also seems to have become less steep across successive generations, says study co-author Anders Fjell, a neuropsychologist at the University of Oslo in Norway.

The findings are “confirmatory” of other studies on the topic, which indicated that the rate of memory decline is slowing down but weren’t statistically significant, says Carol Brayne, an epidemiologist who studies dementia at the University of Cambridge, UK. “It is another piece of the jigsaw.”

Because many populations around the world are ageing — that is, older individuals are becoming a larger proportion of the total population — the number of people living with dementia is increasing worldwide. But an individual person’s risk of dementia at any given age has dropped by two-thirds over the past 40 years in the United States4. “For those who reach 80, a smaller percentage [of people] will get dementia than before,” explains Fjell.

Memory stays strong in old age when this brain enzyme is active

Memory stays strong in old age when this brain enzyme is active

To understand what might be driving this trend, Fjell and his colleagues used longitudinal data on individuals’ cognitive performance to estimate their memory trajectories over time. The authors examined whether people born later in the twentieth century showed differences in their memory performance and their rate of memory decline compared with those born earlier.

The analysis found that with each successive birth decade, people were 64% more likely to maintain stable memory function — that is, experience little or no memory deterioration.

The authors also investigated brain imaging data from nearly 2,000 people over a median of four years. They found that a stable memory during ageing also corresponded to a decrease in shrinkage of the hippocampus — a brain region involved in memory formation.

#1258. Bayern Munich slammed as 'despicable' and accused of 'co-ordinated' plot to undermine Jamal Musiala after club chief questioned star's contract due to his health issues - with Jude Bellingham, Michael Olise and Rio Ferdinand backing the youngster

Published: 10:38 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 11:29 EST, 23 November 2026

Bayern Munich have come under criticism from FIFA's players' union and leading figures in the game amid accusations that the club is attempting to slash Jamal Musiala's wages following his diagnosis with a 'neurological dysfunction'.

The Germany international was diagnosed over the summer with absence seizures, a form of epilepsy which causes 'brief but easily treatable seizures'.

Musiala shocked the sporting world when he collapsed in two matches earlier this season, with Bayern manager Vincent Kompany explaining that the player had suffered from a reaction to a change in his medication.

Comments from members of Bayern's hierarchy have sparked controversy in Germany and abroad, with senior figures appearing to question the length of the player's contract – which runs until 2030 – should Musiala not recover his form.

Honorary president Uli Hoeness was the first to speak out on the potential drop-off in form Musiala might suffer with long-term absences, claiming earlier this month that he 'may never regain the performance level he once had'.

'We are facing a dilemma in this case, as he is suffering from an illness that cannot simply be cured, but it can be controlled to a certain extent with the use of medication,' Hoeness told German outlet BR24.

Fifpro and international footballers have come out in support of Musiala over concerns that Bayern Munich might reduce his salary

Both Uli Hoeness and Karl-Heinz Rummenigge have made comments suggesting consequences should Musiala not return to his level

Jan-Christian Dreesen also suggested that the club would need to 'assess' the situation if his performances do not return to their high heights

Chief executive Jan-Christian Dreesen then backed up Hoeness's comments and implied that Musiala's contract may need to be 'assessed'.

'We're monitoring his level of play. He'll certainly need time to improve further – like any injured player,' Dreesen said in discussion with AZ. 'And then we need to calmly assess the situation and, if necessary, sit down with his family and management.

'Either we'll all be happy together and he'll be the same Jamal he always was – or, if he's a different Jamal along the way, we'll have to discuss it.'

'If we're not consistently at a level that also aligns with the economic realities, then we'll have to talk to each other. Nevertheless, we have a valid contract, and that's the end of it.'

The 23-year-old is one of Bayern's highest-earners, having signed a deal with the club to extend his time in Bavaria in February 2025. The deal is thought to be worth £18.4million per year.

Adding fuel to the fire days later was former CEO Karl-Heinz Rummenigge, who told Sky Sports/RTL that he thought it was almost reasonable to discuss a renegotiation should Musiala not return to the level at which he once played.

'That is certainly possible and cannot be ruled out,' he said. 'Unfortunately, what we know suggests that it will be difficult to reach the level that he has so often shown here in this stadium.'

'We need to talk to the family, the player, and above all, the agency. Because then these sums are – sorry, with all due respect – no longer feasible.

'I can't imagine Jamal leaving the club or another club buying him under these circumstances. That's a problem. I think we handled this very sensitively with the player, and we're all interested in him coming back - ideally in top form. But what happens if that's not the case? Then we'll still have to think about the finances. And that's a task that the board and the supervisory board unfortunately have to make.'

Rummenigge added that he did not think it was 'problematic' for these discussions to be happening publicly, due to the club's interest in 'him coming back and playing well'.

But the player union Fifpro were forthright in their disagreement with his statements,  releasing a statement claiming that all parties currently sharing their views on Musiala's contract 'should know better'.

'Bayern's honorary president, chief executive and former chief executive have all publicly questioned Musiala's contract in quick succession,' the statement read.

'In Fifpro's view, this is a co-ordinated strategy to put pressure on Musiala and his representatives ahead of any negotiations. A club of Bayern's standing should know better.'

When this statement was shared to social media via journalist Fabrizio Romano, global talents including Jude Bellingham and Musiala's team-mate Michael Olise were among those to like the post.

Musiala collapsed on the pitch at two consecutive games in August (pictured being helped by team-mates against RB Leipzig)

The 23-year-old has been diagnosed with absence seizures and is managing his medication

Vincent Kompany has been supportive of his player's struggles, and took him off the bench with some success last weekend

Rio Ferdinand elaborated on those comments in a more detailed post on social media, adding that he believed the club are 'better than this'.

'If they want to negotiate more reasonable terms for the club going forward due to the health issues Jamal has, then surely speak to him and his team rather than to the media,' Ferdinand wrote on X. 'This situation must be hard enough to deal with for Jamal without the media and club officials talking about it publicly.

'Bayern Munich are one of the clubs who from afar have always carried themselves with a class and standard that most have admired. Sadly, this just doesn't feel like Bayern Munich in this situation.'

Criticisms were even more fiery in Germany, with the vice president of Germany's player union Michael Franz accusing the club of harassment.

'What the Bayern Munich officials are doing, and I don't mean Kompany and (Max) Eberl (director of sport), who have behaved impeccably, seems despicable to me,' Franz shared in an interview with Sport1. 'There is even something about it that resembles harassment.'

'A footballer's level of performance can be discussed publicly, but it is not right to talk about his illness and the salary he receives in such circumstances. We must not forget that Jamal Musiala has done everything in his power to come back.'

'Money has become more important than the person, and that is unacceptable.'

Former Bayern captain Stefan Effenberg stressed how important 'support and protection' from the club towards their players is, particularly for those in greater need like Musiala.

'We are talking about someone who is suffering from an illness. What I would have expected is for the club's senior officials to apologise,' Effenberg said, adding that he thought that the communications from the club had been 'disastrous'.

Musiala collapsed twice within four days in mid-August, first during Bayern's match against Leipzig – shortly after scoring – and then against Heidenheim.

He then returned to the pitch in September, netting against Bodo/Glimt in Champions League action and Union Berlin shortly before the first international break.

After suffering a hamstring injury, Musiala then spent time away from the side before his return at the end of last week – a match which also saw Harry Kane suffer an ankle injury which will keep him out for over three months.

Fifpro's statement went on to add that Bayern must be careful with their player's mental wellbeing as well as his physical issues.

'Bayern has a duty of care to Musiala,' the statement continued. 'Across professional football, uncertainty about a player's future can take a toll on their mental health, particularly when they are recovering from injury.

'Making Musiala's health and future a matter of public debate adds to that pressure. Any concerns about his contract should be raised privately with him and his representatives.

'Contracts are there to be respected. An injury or a dip in form gives a club no grounds to reopen terms it agreed to, just as a run of outstanding performances gives a player no automatic right to a pay rise.'

#1257. Arsenal Fans Slam ‘Abysmal’ Dud in Borussia Dortmund Draw

In their fifth Champions League game of the season, Arsenal hosted Borussia Dortmund. They had to settle for a point on the night as the match ended 1-1.

The Gunners had won all but one of their games in Europe so far this term, and carried their impressive form into the early stages of this encounter. Having been trusted to start ahead of Kai Havertz, Viktor Gyokeres started brilliantly, smashing the ball in from 25 yards to give Arsenal a lead after just 10 minutes.

That was enough to separatethe teams at the break, but Dortmund were able to draw level 10 minutes into the second half. Maxi Beier showed great composure to find the bottom corner after being set up well by Joane Gadou.

That was enough to see the game end all square at 1-1.

Leny Yoro was sent off in the eighth minute, ruining United's chances from the offset.

Arsenal signed Christos Tzolis from Club Brugge on a five-year deal in the summer, as the winger was brought in to help fill the void left by the departing Leandro Trossard and Gabriel Martinelli. There were also hopes of signing another high-profile attacker, like Vinicius Junior, one of the best wingers in the world, but no elite forward arrived.

This meant Tzolis came straight into the starting XI, and he looked bright early on, getting two assists on debut in the Community Shield win over Manchester City. He then picked up assists against Napoli and Chelsea but is yet to score for the Gunners – or register a goal contribution since August.

Against Dortmund, he was poor, struggling to make a big impact. Mikel Arteta preferred Eberechi Eze in the Premier League draw against Newcastle United, and he lost patience with an ineffective Tzolis after 65 minutes in the Champions League, hooking him for the Englishman.

His 6.3 SofaScore rating was the lowest of any starting Arsenal player, as the winger finished the match with 64% passing accuracy, 0/2 attempted crosses, 1/3 shots on target, and lost the ball 16 times.

Fans watching on were far from impressed with Tzolis' efforts. Making their feelings clear, one wrote: "Tzolis had a good 3 games and been mediocre ever since, if we being real."

Another added: "Tzolis is genuinely so bad." A third wrote: "Tzolis, I’ve been holding my tongue but he really can’t hang."

Another wrote: "Should have taken Tzolis off at half time. He has been abysmal."

One more summed up the mood, writing: "Tzolis plays like a pitch invader." While a final fan said: "Tzolis just isn't on the same wavelength as the rest of the team man."

#1255. What Steven Gerrard Really Thought of MLS After LA Galaxy Stint

There has long been a debate about the true quality of Major League Soccer. Thomas Muller recently caused a stir when he spoke about his issues with the United States' premier football competition.

The former Bayern Munich star, currently with Vancouver Whitecaps, has spent just over 12 months playing for the Canadian club and has outlined his main issue with MLS. He claimed there isn't enough pressure for players due to a lack of jeopardy when it comes to relegation:

"There is no big pressure. There is... 'oh yeah we do a rebuild'. Nobody's happy to lose, but it's totally different when you're fighting relegation.

"You lose budget for the next year, you lose people working at the club when the budget changes. It's totally different for fans. The pressure... the players maybe have no contracts for next year when you go down.

"So the playing style changes when you play a bottom of the league team in Europe. They fight for their lives. And sometimes I have the feeling... because of the system, the playing style is a bit more optimistic or careless defensively. That's maybe good for seeing some nice offensive plays when the games are opening up."

The comments quickly went viral, sparking much debate about where MLS ranks among the best leagues in world football. With that in mind, it's interesting to learn what Steven Gerrard thought of MLS during his stint at LA Galaxy.

The former LA Galaxy once gave his thoughts on the MLS.

Gerrard is one of the greatest English footballers of all time. He spent almost his entire career at Liverpool – famously winning the 2005 Champions League – before moving to MLS for his final few years. Between 2015 and 2016, the midfielder played 39 games for LA Galaxy before retiring at the age of 36.

Speaking after the end of his first MLS season in the United States, Gerrard concluded that the competition was "a lot better than I initially thought." He claimed it was no 'retirement league', explaining:

"If people think they can come here just to have a holiday and retire, they are going to have a mistake because they won't perform well and they won't do their team justice because I have had to come here and work hard and get fit, make sure that I keep performing to play well."

"A lot of people talk about the MLS, about the level, but for me a lot of them are wrong. Until you come here and sample it yourself, you see how strong it is and how fit and professional the players are.

"Every single game is a different challenge, certainly on the road you come up against places and teams where it is very hot and very humid; some teams play on astroturf. So each game is very tricky and very difficult. The games at home, we've had a very strong team and we've enjoyed some really strong performances."

Gerrard concluded: "You know a lot of TV channels all around the world have started to follow the MLS. A lot of big players from Europe have come over to try and strengthen the league. I am sure with time it will be continuing to grow and become a lot stronger."

While Muller may well have a point about the league needing more jeopardy, it's interesting to learn that a player of Gerrard's quality held MLS in such high regard.

He wasn't the first iconic Englishman to play for LA Galaxy, with David Beckham paving the way on that front. However, Gerrard lasted only 39 games, compared to Beckham's 124. Truthfully, the Liverpool legend struggled to bring his best form to the US, which perhaps explains why he retired not that long after arriving.

We want to hear from you. Share your perspective in the comments below, and please keep the conversation respectful.

City’s run of seven league wins in a row always looked in danger here against a vibrant and energetic Villa. Maresca will also reflect on two poor goals conceded after errors from Marc Guéhi and goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma.

#1253. The World Cup RETURNS to America! FIFA announces 2031 tournament hosts after historic four-country bid

By ISABEL BALDWIN, US ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR

Published: 10:23 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 13:19 EST, 23 November 2026

The World Cup is set to return to America after FIFA awarded the 2031 women's tournament to a historic four-nation bid.

Following the success of the men's tournament this summer, the United States was announced as one of the hosts of the women's edition in five years' time during a virtual meeting of FIFA's national associations on Monday.

The US will co-host the global soccer extravaganza alongside Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica after the four countries' joint bid was awarded uncontested the 2031 tournament.

The selection marks a milestone for the Women's World Cup with the tournament being hosted across four nations for the first time in its history.

The last World Cup was co-hosted by multiple countries for the first time with the 2023 edition taking place across Australia and New Zealand.

This summer's men's World Cup was also co-hosted by the US with games taking place across the States, Canada and Mexico.

The World Cup is set to return to the United States for the 2031 women's edition of the event

Spain are reigning champions after winning the Women's World Cup in 2023

The United States Women's National Team are four-time winners in 1991, 1999, 2015 and 2019

The 2031 tournament will also be the largest in the competition's history, featuring an expanded 48-team field and 104 matches for the first time.

'We are incredibly honored and excited to welcome the world to the United States, Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica for the 2031 FIFA Women's World Cup,' said US Soccer President Cindy Parlow Cone.

'This is a historic moment for our four countries, but the opportunity is much bigger than any one of us. Together with FIFA, we want to deliver the biggest and most impactful Women's World Cup in history and use its success to accelerate the growth of women's soccer around the world. Our ambition is to create a tournament that not only inspires millions of players, but helps give them the opportunities to play, grow and pursue their dreams.'

The selection marks the third time that the Women's World Cup has been awarded to the US with the country previously hosting the landmark 1999 and 2003 editions alone. The national team's tournament win in 1999 was the second of its four titles.

Meanwhile, Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica will become first-time hosts at the historic tournament.

'This milestone furthers the continued belief that the best days of soccer in America are still ahead,' said U.S. Soccer CEO and General Secretary JT Batson.

'We have an opportunity to use the momentum from the 2031 FIFA Women's World Cup to accelerate our ambitions for the future of soccer, from expanding access and participation to strengthening the pathways that develop the next generation of players. We are excited to work alongside our partners across the region to make this tournament a defining moment for women's soccer.'

The U.S.-led 2031 project across the CONCACAF regional soccer body bid offers FIFA a choice of stadiums in 20 cities: 14 in the U.S., four in Mexico plus San José in Costa Rica and Kingston, Jamaica.

US Soccer President Cindy Parlow Cone said the federation was honored to be selected

The host selection of the 2035 Women's World Cup was awarded to a joint bid between England, Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales

The host selection of the 2035 Women's World Cup was also announced on Monday with the tournament being awarded to another joint bid between England, Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales.

It marks the first time that a World Cup has been hosted on the British Isles since the men's tournament in 1966 in England.

The United Kingdom bid joins England with Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales that offers a choice from 19 venues, including Wembley Stadium in London.

The winning candidates and FIFA president Gianni Infantino promised commercially successful tournaments - the first editions with 48 teams and 104 games - and to reinvest all that money in women's soccer.

FIFA wanted these heavyweights of women's soccer to face no opposition without rival bids and so lead hosting the first expanded tournaments. That will bring parity with the men's World Cup which expanded to 48 teams this year in the US, Canada and Mexico.

The 2027 Women's World Cup will have 32 teams in Brazil.

#1251. Paul Scholes Named Man Utd Icon as Best Striker He Played With During His Career

Paul Scholes has revealed that Ruud van Nistelrooy was the best striker he shared the pitch with during his career. Scholes spent all 19 seasons of his senior career under Sir Alex Ferguson at Manchester United, where he made 714 appearances, scored 153 goals and provided another 83 assists. Those achievements have helped cement his reputation as one of the greatest players to have ever put on the red jersey of Man United.

During his time at Old Trafford, Scholes helped the Red Devils win 26 trophies, including 11 Premier League titles and two Champions League crowns, a haul that ranks him among the most decorated players in football history. He became renowned for his exceptional vision and range of passing, regularly delivering the ball with remarkable accuracy, timing and precision, traits that place him among the greatest midfielders of the Premier League era.

Scholes had the opportunity to play with some of the greatest strikers Man United have ever had throughout his career, from Andy Cole and Dwight Yorke to Eric Cantona and the club's record goalscorer, Wayne Rooney. Even so, none developed the same on-field understanding with him as Dutch striker van Nistelrooy.

Although he played alongside a number of Manchester United icons, Scholes explained to BBC Sounds during an episode of 606 Savage Social that one player stood out as the teammate he had a much stronger on-pitch connection with above all others.

Speaking about van Nistelrooy, Scholes described a natural understanding between the pair. He knew where the striker would make his runs and precisely when to play the pass to give his Dutch teammate the clearest chance of scoring.

"That's an easy one. I don't want to disrespect any of the other forwards - because I've played with some amazing players, especially at United. Andy Cole, Dwight Yorke, Ole Gunnar [Solskjaer] at the time, but I always thought I had the best connection with Ruud van Nistelrooy. I played the season with him, and I think I scored 20 goals playing as a ten. I knew what he wanted, I knew the runs he'd make and where he wanted the ball. What a finisher. That man was just hungry. His life depended on scoring goals. He was the one I felt I had a great connection with."

He ignored Lionel Messi, Ronaldo Nazario and so many legends to name someone he played with - but it wasn't Cristiano Ronaldo.

Scholes and van Nistelrooy played together 165 times and combined for 16 goal contributions, during the Dutchman's five seasons at Old Trafford. Nevertheless, he made a significant mark on both the club and English football, scoring 95 goals and adding 14 assists across 150 Premier League appearances. He also claimed the Golden Boot and Player of the Season awards in 2002/03.

His record is one reason he is so often regarded as one of the greatest strikers in Premier League history. Few forwards seemed so completely devoted to finding the net, making his relatively short spell in English football a disappointment for fans who wanted to see more.

#1249. Supercomputer Predicts 2026-27 Championship Table

The final 2026/27 Championship table has been predicted in full by a Supercomputer following the opening months of the new season.

West Ham United, Burnley and Wolverhampton Wanderers dropped into English football's second tier after suffering relegation from the Premier League last season. That trio - which, for the first time in four years, was not made up of the same three clubs that had won promotion the season before - will all be desperate to bounce straight back at the first attempt.

Meanwhile, Lincoln City, Cardiff City and Bolton Wanderers would surely be more than content with consolidation after securing their Championship status on the back of impressive League One campaigns. For those clubs, simply keeping their heads above water and establishing themselves at a higher level may be viewed as success.

However, if the Supercomputer's projections, courtesy of Opta (as of 24/11/26), are to be believed, there could be plenty of twists and turns ahead. The Championship rarely follows a script and has a habit of throwing up surprises when least expected, and this predicted final table suggests several clubs may be in for a rollercoaster ride. In fact, the standings look markedly different from how many supporters and pundits would have expected the season to unfold.

Preston North End have been perennial mid-table finishers in the Championship for over a decade. However, after a dismal start to the 2026/27 campaign, Opta's Supercomputer thinks they will finish rock bottom this campaign and drop to League One alongside Derby County and Watford.

Lincoln City are riding the crest of promotion, but it is set to be a tough campaign for them, having lost manager Michael Skubala to Bristol City in the off-season. Wins against Bolton, Bristol City, Preston and Burnley helped put them up into a much safer predicted position initially, but a 4-0 thrashing at the hands of Charlton has them hovering just above the bottom three.

Burnley, who were relegated from the Premier League in 25/26, are expected to finish 20th with just 49 points. That would be a huge disappointment for the Lancashire side, who would have had aspirations of returning to England's top tier at the first time of asking.

Charlton Athletic enjoyed a tremendous start to the 2026/27 campaign, picking up victories against Derby County, West Ham United and Preston. They couldn't maintain that incredible run, though, plummeting down the table following an 11-match winless run. After beating Sheffield United and Lincoln, they now sit slightly higher up the table.

Bolton Wanderers are back in the Championship following a long time away. After winning five of their opening 16 games, they're expected to avoid relegation.

After coming from 4-1 down to beat Burnley 5-4, Cardiff City have lost their following two games. They are not expected to finish 16th, one place above Bristol City.

The Robins have firmly established themselves in the English second tier, qualifying for the playoffs in the 2024/25 season. However, despite success in recent years, the Supercomputer thinks they will struggle and finish in the bottom half.

Blackburn Rovers have flirted with relegation in recent years, with fans of the club regularly venting their frustration with their owners, the Venky's. They always find a way to escape the drop, though, and are expected to have more than enough to stay up once again this season.

Millwall came so close to achieving promotion to England's top tier in 2025/26, eventually having to settle for third place and a spot in the playoffs. Opta's Supercomputer thinks they will just miss out on a playoff berth this time round.

Wrexham narrowly failed to make the playoffs last season as they finished seventh. After a very slow start to the season, they are again expected to miss out, with the Supercomputer predicting them to finish in a disappointing 13th with 64 points.

Portsmouth were at threat of relegation in the 2025/26 campaign, but they avoided the drop after improving in the final months. They've had an impressive start to the campaign and are being predicted to finish in the top half, having just beaten West Ham.

Sheffield United endured a torrid campaign in 25/26. At one point, it looked as if they would have a battle on their hands to maintain their Championship status. They eventually finished mid-table, and they are predicted to end this campaign in a similar position.

The 2026/27 season will be the first year in which six teams qualify for the playoffs, expanded from four.

Norwich City ended the 2025/26 campaign on fire and would have been expecting to start 26/27 in the same manner. After an awful start to the campaign, they've recovered and now occupy 11th place in the real table. The Supercomputer thinks they'll end up finishing one spot higher, but still just outside the playoff places.

Swansea City had an electric start to the season and led the way after 10 matches. However, after just one win in their seven matches, they are now predicted to finish ninth with 70 points.

Queens Park Rangers have had a decent start to the campaign, picking up 28 points from their opening 17 matches. The Supercomputer thinks they'll fall short in their bid to make the playoffs, though.

Stoke City spent big in the 2026 summer transfer window, with Ethan Galbraith and George Hirst among the players who arrived for big money. Their decision to spend big has paid dividends so far, with the club currently flying high in third. The Supercomputer thinks they'll just about scrape into the playoffs, though.

West Ham, the favourites in the eyes of many to win the Championship and return to the Premier League at the first time of asking before a ball was kicked, had an awful start to the campaign. They failed to win their opening three matches, with draws against Burnley and Watford, as well as a 2-1 defeat to Charlton at the London Stadium.

The Hammers climbed up the table after that poor start, but after their form took another turn for the worse once more, Nuno Espirito Santo lost his job in early November and was replaced by Scott Parker. After going winless in Parker's first four matches in charge, they are now expected to miss out on an automatic promotion berth.

Tom Brady is no longer at Birmingham City, but the Blues are still expected to have a shot at promotion this season. They are being tipped to finish the campaign in fourth with 76 points, one place above Midlands rivals West Bromwich Albion.

Southampton started the campaign on -4 points after they were punished for spying on several other teams in the 2025/26 campaign. Despite that disadvantage, the Supercomputer thinks the Saints will finish third after winning nine of their opening 17 matches.

Wolverhampton Wanderers boast an enviable mix of youthful excitement and older, wiser players, so with the resources at their disposal, it would be a shock if they didn't get that automatic promotion place. The Supercomputer thinks they will just about seal their return to the Premier League at the first time of asking.

Middlesbrough, who were beaten by Hull City in the playoff final in May, will be delighted if they don't have to go through the playoffs again this term as they chase a return to the Premier League. Despite dropping points to Watford in their last outing, Kim Hellberg's side are predicted to be crowned champions with 82 points.

#1248. Genoa defender Ostigard spends night in hospital with high fever

Genoa defender Leo Ostigard spent Monday night in hospital after suffering a sudden high fever, although tests have since ruled out anything serious.

According to ANSA, the Norway international was taken to Genoa’s San Martino Hospital in the early hours, after the fever came with a severe headache.

He was examined by infectious disease specialist Professor Matteo Bassetti and his team. The routine diagnostic tests came back reassuring and ruled out any significant medical problems. Ostigard will nonetheless remain under observation at the hospital for the rest of today.

The scare came just a day after one of his best performances of the season. Ostigard was among Genoa’s standout players as Daniele De Rossi’s side won 2-0 at Sassuolo on Sunday, with Milutin Osmajić scoring both goals and the defence keeping a clean sheet.

That result made it three wins in four league games for the Grifone, who are 10th on 16 points.

Genoa will hope to have their defender back for a demanding week. They visit Inter at San Siro on Saturday at 20:45 CET [19:45 GMT], before facing the Nerazzurri again in the Coppa Italia next Tuesday.

#1247. Frick promises his Dons will maintain their positive approach and go on the attack in Ibrox clash

By CALUM CROWE, SCOTTISH DEPUTY CHIEF SPORTS WRITER

Published: 13:28 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 13:41 EST, 23 November 2026

Aberdeen  boss Mario Frick has vowed to go on the attack when his new-look team take on Rangers at Ibrox tomorrow night.

Appointed as the club's new manager during the international break, Frick's reign got off to a flyer as Aberdeen won 4-2 away at Kilmarnock on Saturday.

Renowned for a high-octane attacking style of play at his previous clubs, the 52-year-old Liechtensteiner has already generated a wave of positivity at Pittodrie.

Aberdeen will face a tough task against an in-form Rangers side who are unbeaten in their last 13 matches.

But Frick insists there is no prospect of his team turning up at Ibrox and parking the bus in their efforts to take a positive result.

'I'm looking forward to it and I'm pretty confident in our squad,' he said. 'Now we have to prove that and have another good performance.

'That's not our style (to sit in and defend). We want to play like we did at Kilmarnock. That's our style of play.

Frick is all smiles after his side put four goals past Kilmarnock in his first match in charge

'Rangers will be a tough game. They are very strong, especially at home. I saw a lot of quality, particularly in their forward areas.

'We have to defend better than we did on Saturday, that's for sure, and that's what we're working on.

'I have to get to know my players even better because it's only been a week since we arrived in Aberdeen, and that takes time.

'But, of course, it helps when you win the first game. We've got some confidence now and I'm pretty confident we can take something from Ibrox.

'At the weekend, you could see that the mentality is very good. We struggled during the first 20 minutes of the second half, but the substitutes were very good and had a huge impact.

'I think, in the end, it was a deserved win and now we're looking forward to meeting Rangers at Ibrox.

'Defensively, we have to improve. Otherwise, it will be very difficult. I'm pretty sure we can defend better.

'But, like I say, we want to play like we did at the weekend. It's not our style (just to sit back and defend).'

Kevin Nisbet is mobbed by team-mates after netting the first of his double at Rugby Park

After the doom and gloom of the Stephen Robinson era, Frick has immediately created a feelgood factor at Aberdeen.

The fans were singing his name after the victory at Rugby Park on Saturday - and he wants to strengthen that feeling of unity throughout the club.

'It's been very good so far, especially with the win,' he added. 'The team has some confidence now and I see many players laughing.

'That's very important because we do this for fun as well. When you go onto the pitch, you have to take things seriously, but always with enjoyment. That's very important.

'The relationship between the team and the supporters is important, not between the supporters and me, because the team is the most important thing.

'For the players' confidence, it was very important that so many supporters travelled to Kilmarnock and celebrated the win with us. That was the first step.

'It's not the time for me to make a statement. It's the first time we're playing together at Ibrox, and it's important that we stick to our style of play.

'That's the most important thing to me. It is an exciting game and we are looking forward to it.'
